analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by an incorrect end-of-buffer allowance in the slow-path sequence copier. ZSTD_execSequenceEnd() computes `oend_w = oend - WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` and then calls ZSTD_safecopy() for literals and match copies. But ZSTD_safecopy() is documented/implemented to allow writes up to 16 bytes past `oend_w`, which means it can write past the real `oend` when used with `oend_w = oend - WILDCOPY_OVERLENGTH` in this end-of-buffer path. With crafted sequence lengths near block end, the final `while (op < oend) *op++ = *ip++` in ZSTD_safecopy() overruns the destination heap buffer (ASan write at line 753).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The fuzzed frame reaches zstd block sequence decoding through blosc frame decompression, with malformed sequence/literal metadata such that execution takes ZSTD_execSequenceEnd() (near-end slow path) and performs safecopy close to output end. A small output buffer (176-byte allocation in this run) plus sequence parameters that place copy boundaries near `oend` trigger a write past the allocated destination by a few bytes (2 bytes in this PoV), producing the heap-buffer-overflow in ZSTD_safecopy().
